topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the core learning objectives concerning cancer treatment approaches.

topics.label: Conventional cancer treatments and cytotoxic drug resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore traditional modalities—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with systemic toxicity and efflux-mediated drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cancer vulnerabilities and repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on therapeutic strategies designed to exploit inherent cancer cell vulnerabilities, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and defective DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine small-molecule therapies targeting hyperactivated oncogenic kinases and the molecular mechanisms that lead to treatment resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe engineered antibody therapeutics designed to block surface receptor signaling, trigger immune cytotoxicity, or deliver targeted cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and cellular engineering
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the role of immune surveillance and the development of immunotherapies, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific T-cell engagers, and CAR T-cell therapy.

topics.label: Overall challenges, future directions, and therapeutic dilemmas
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine broader clinical challenges in oncology, including historical trends in mortality, future paradigms in personalized medicine and detection, and ethical dilemmas in clinical trial design.
